Own digest: Paper card. Question: How do the electrical and magnetic properties of high-entropy oxides (HEOs) correlate with their composition and configurational entropy?. System: [LaNd](Cr0.2Mn0.2Fe0.2Co0.2Ni0.2)O3 perovskites. Processing: solid-state reactions, with initial components mixed in stoichiometric proportions, ground for 3 h, compacted at 3 tons/cm2, and heated at 1300 °C for 10 h. Test conditions: temperatures of 150-450 K, frequencies of 10−1-107 Hz, and magnetic fields of ±3T. Question: How can strong local compositional disorder in high entropy oxides be exploited to generate tunable magnetic behaviors, ranging from macroscopically ordered states to frustration-driven dynamic spin interactions, and can a simplified model predict the emergence of these states?. System: La(Cr0.2Mn0.2Fe0.2Co0.2Ni0.2)O3 (L5BO) and Mn-varied variants La(Cr0.15Mn0.4Fe0.15Co0.15Ni0.15)O3 (40% Mn) and La(Cr0.1Mn0.6Fe0.1Co0.1Ni0.1)O3 (60% Mn). Processing: Pulsed laser epitaxy (PLD) on SrTiO3 (STO) and (La0.3Sr0.7)(Al0.65Ta0.35)O3 (LSAT) substrates; films were single-phase, epitaxial, with thicknesses of 56 nm (40% Mn), 58 nm (60% Mn), 62 nm (20% Mn), and ~90 nm for neutron diffraction.. Test conditions: Neutron diffraction on single-crystal films and bulk powder; SQUID magnetometry (field-cooled vs. zero-field-cooled) from low temperatures up to 300 K; Monte Carlo simulations using a classical Heisenberg model..
